deities: Shri Shirdi Sai Baba (main murti on the first floor)
Ten avatars of Lord Vishnu (paintings in the temple)

history.period: Built 2010; opened to the public 3 November 2010
history.summary: NOTE - POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: this entry documents the Sai Mandir at Assangthang, Namchi, a two-storeyed Shirdi Sai Baba temple built in 2010 and opened on 3 November 2010 as a gift of then Chief Minister Pawan Chamling to the people of Sikkim. The main statue of Shirdi Sai Baba stands on the first floor; the ground floor accommodates devotees for hymn-singing and prayer, and the walls carry ten paintings depicting the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu. The temple is set in a garden with a panoramic view of Mt Kanchenjunga and has a calm atmosphere for meditation. CSV row 905 ('Shirdi Sai Baba Mandir Namchi') is being researched by another agent and may describe this same shrine - flagging for dedup rather than treating them as two temples. Sources disagree on timings (8 AM-5 PM vs 7 AM-7 PM) - verify before visiting.

name: Sai Mandir
town_description: Namchi is the headquarters of Namchi district (South Sikkim), about 78 km from Gangtok. The Sai Mandir stands in the Assangthang area (near Singithang, Apatan Marg), about 3 km from Char Dham and 5 km from the Namchi taxi stand.

travel.airport: Bagdogra Airport, West Bengal, about 102 km from Namchi; Pakyong Airport near Gangtok is closer by air distance (verify).
travel.railway: New Jalpaiguri (NJP) Station, West Bengal, about 96 km from Namchi.
travel.road: Reached by road from Namchi town (taxi/auto); about 3 km from the Solophok Char Dham complex and 5 km from the Namchi taxi stand.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May and October to December for clear mountain views.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM by trawell.in and 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM by travelsetu.com - verify before visiting. Entry is free.
